description: A doctor faces a profound ethical dilemma: sacrifice one healthy patient to save five critically ill patients, or allow the five critically ill patients to die, thereby preserving the life of the healthy individual.
actions: Harvest organs from the healthy patient
Do not harvest organs from the healthy patient
background: Five patients are critically ill and will die without immediate organ transplants.
One patient is perfectly healthy and would die if their organs are harvested.
No other viable options exist to save the five critically ill patients.
The situation is final and irreversible; a choice must be made.
consequences: If organs are harvested: One healthy patient dies, five critically ill patients live.
If organs are not harvested: One healthy patient lives, five critically ill patients die.
patients: The one healthy patient (potential involuntary donor)
The five critically ill patients (potential recipients)
